name: Escape Chill Dog
summary: Leaving Chill Dog from the bottom is a controlled guard reset: release the neck-cleared high-leg connection and restore inside frames.
description: Leaving Chill Dog from bottom opens the neck-cleared rubber-guard connection and restores inside frames. Escaping that control from top is a separate task.
overview:
The bottom player is already facing the opponent in Chill Dog, with a high rubber-guard leg connection. The bottom player owns Chill Dog rather than being trapped in a turtle ride. An escape from the high guard by the top player is a different action.

The bottom player is on the back or hip with a high rubber-guard leg across the upper back. One of the top player's arms is isolated beside the bottom player rather than framing inside. Release any wrist, neck or elbow loading before opening the high-leg enclosure. Lower the controlling leg through a comfortable hip angle rather than pulling the foot against the knee.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Brandon McCaghren — Gogoplata from rubber guard](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wn39-wrfsbs); [Eddie Bravo — Chill Dog / Invisible Collar clarification](https://www.10thplanetjj.com/forum/threads/17657-Chill-Dog-Invisible-Collar-Question).

attacker.description: Escape Chill Dog (attacker): The bottom player is on the back or hip with a high rubber-guard leg across the upper back. One of the top player's arms is isolated beside the bottom player rather than framing inside. Release any wrist, neck or elbow loading before opening the high-leg enclosure.
attacker.overview:
The bottom player is already facing the opponent in Chill Dog, with a high rubber-guard leg connection. The bottom player owns Chill Dog rather than being trapped in a turtle ride. An escape from the high guard by the top player is a different action.

The bottom player is on the back or hip with a high rubber-guard leg across the upper back. One of the top player's arms is isolated beside the bottom player rather than framing inside. Release any wrist, neck or elbow loading before opening the high-leg enclosure. Lower the controlling leg through a comfortable hip angle rather than pulling the foot against the knee.

Bring the forearms and knees between the bodies as space becomes available. Keep the shoulders and hips oriented toward the opponent while re-establishing a comfortable facing guard. Check posture, knee comfort and inside space before resuming a sweep or submission attack.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

After fully releasing the high-leg connection, use a small hip escape to restore inside frames and knees. This guard retention keeps a facing passer from advancing while ordinary guard is rebuilt.

As the high leg comes down, place a forearm inside the approaching shoulder to prevent a crossface and renewed chest pressure. Keep that frame while the hips make room for the returning knee; opening the leg without protecting this space invites a pin.

flashcards.question: Escape Chill Dog (bottom): What are you releasing in this bottom-seat escape?
flashcards.answer: The bottom player owns Chill Dog. This reset opens that facing high guard rather than escaping from a turtle ride.
flashcards.answer_line: Your neck-cleared guard and arm trap

plausible: High leg only; shoulder wrap loaded
Overhook only; head stays enclosed
trap: Head-side hand only; knee hug stays

flashcards.question: Escape Chill Dog (bottom): Which load must come off before the leg lowers?
flashcards.answer: Release the loaded arm-and-neck connection before lowering the high leg so the movement does not drag a fixed joint.

plausible: Only free-foot pressure on the mat
Only overhook; neck stays cinched
trap: Only leg squeeze; wrist still pulled

flashcards.question: Escape Chill Dog (bottom): How do you lower the high leg without twisting the knee?
flashcards.answer: Lower the leg through a comfortable hip angle; avoid pulling the foot while the knee is fixed against the opponent.
flashcards.answer_line: Turn your hip; guide high leg down

plausible: Stay flat; drag the ankle sideways
Fix hip; straighten the trapped leg
trap: Pull foot down before turning hip

flashcards.question: Escape Chill Dog (bottom): What replaces the leg as their shoulder comes forward?
flashcards.answer: As Chill Dog opens, put the forearm inside the approaching shoulder and recover knee space to resist chest access.

plausible: Both hands chase behind their head
Old high leg hangs loosely behind

flashcards.question: Escape Chill Dog (bottom): How should chest and knees align during the facing reset?
flashcards.answer: Maintain a facing orientation while recovering the knees, so the reset remains guard retention rather than back exposure.
flashcards.answer_line: Chest faces them; knees come inside

plausible: Chest away; both knees trail
Chest down; knees tucked underneath
trap: Chest faces them; knees stay outside

flashcards.question: Escape Chill Dog (bottom): Their chest enters as the leg drops; what is missing?
flashcards.answer: Opening the high leg is incomplete if chest pressure fills the gap; restore the shoulder frame and make space with the hips.
flashcards.answer_line: Frame holding space for inside knee

plausible: Grip your unsupported foot tighter
Reach farther over their back
trap: Pull knee in without shoulder frame

flashcards.question: Escape Chill Dog (bottom): What shows the arm isolation has already failed?
flashcards.answer: An inside elbow becomes a useful frame again, so abandon the failing Chill Dog trap and recover ordinary guard if needed.

plausible: Their hand stays outside on the mat
Your knee hug stays over their arm
trap: Free hand frames; caught elbow out

flashcards.question: Escape Chill Dog (bottom): Why use a short shrimp after releasing the clinch?
flashcards.answer: Lateral hip movement creates room for guard recovery after the high connection is released; it does not require a reversal.
flashcards.answer_line: Make knee room behind forearm frame

plausible: Bridge up without moving hips aside
Regain head grip before knee space
trap: Bring knee in as the forearm folds

flashcards.question: Escape Chill Dog (bottom): What confirms a facing reset without assuming half guard?
flashcards.answer: Inside knees and forearms restore a facing guard barrier after the high leg opens. This does not automatically capture one opposing leg in half guard; check which lower-leg connections remain.
flashcards.answer_line: Facing them, knees and forearms in

plausible: High leg open, so one leg is caught
Head up, so ankles must be crossed
trap: High leg open; near knee outside

flashcards.question: Escape Chill Dog (top): Which arm should stay available as the guard opens?
flashcards.answer: Use the free arm to maintain inside space while keeping the previously isolated elbow from drifting farther away.
flashcards.answer_line: The free arm as an inside frame

plausible: Trapped arm reaches across the mat
Both arms reach around their back
trap: Free arm outside; caught arm frames

flashcards.question: Escape Chill Dog (top): Which cue means the upper-body control still exists?
flashcards.answer: A remaining knee hug and cleared head-side arm can still retain Chill Dog even if the free leg has moved.
flashcards.answer_line: Knee hug holds; head-side arm clear

plausible: Their knees return between bodies
Both your elbows frame freely inside
trap: Foot on hip, high leg already down

flashcards.question: Escape Chill Dog (top): What should you deny before their free leg climbs?
flashcards.answer: Keep early inside space so the free leg cannot reinforce the high clinch behind your head.

plausible: Their foot settles beside the hip
Their knee returns below your chest
trap: Its crossing low behind your waist

flashcards.question: Escape Chill Dog (top): How should you retrieve the isolated arm?
flashcards.answer: The opening must free the shoulder enough for a controlled elbow recovery; pulling against a fixed leg is not a release.
flashcards.answer_line: After slack, bring elbow toward ribs

plausible: Pull hand first; elbow stays outside
Extend arm to enlarge the leg loop
trap: Pull elbow in once only wrist clears

flashcards.question: Escape Chill Dog (top): When is upright posture available?
flashcards.answer: Raise head and chest progressively once the upper-body control is clear, then address the guard that remains.

plausible: Knees widen despite a tight loop
Free foot down; high leg holds
